MEASURED_SIZING_not_estimated.constraint: TIME, not memory — and it had not been costed

ORACLE_F_REPORTED_BESIDE_IT.definition: the fraction of fills the oracle would decline
ORACLE_F_REPORTED_BESIDE_IT.why: a ceiling reachable only by declining 40% of the book is a different proposition from one reachable at 1%

PRIMARY_STATISTIC.definition: the sum of |P&L| over fills whose P&L is NEGATIVE, per coin-hour
PRIMARY_STATISTIC.name: V_oracle
reported_as: percentage of that cell's maker P&L
PRIMARY_STATISTIC.why: MODEL-FREE, and exactly the CEILING any overlay could reach on that book. V_oracle near zero means NO POLICY COULD HAVE PAID, which closes the line for the right reason rather than because this policy did not.
PRIMARY_STATISTIC.why_percentage: the only form comparable across cells of different size

TAIL_EXCLUDED_r_IS_PER_CELL_NEVER_GLOBAL: a global tail excludes the whole survey's largest fills, which concentrate in whichever cells happen to be extreme, so a global r_ex answers a question about the POOLED book rather than about whether ANY CELL clears break-even

WHAT_COUNTS_declared_now_for_the_NEW_sta.closes_the_overlay_line: the 90th percentile of V_oracle below 1% of maker P&L — near zero everywhere, meaning no policy could have paid
WHAT_COUNTS_declared_now_for_the_NEW_sta.indeterminate: anything between, reported as indeterminate rather than argued either way
WHAT_COUNTS_declared_now_for_the_NEW_sta.the_overlay_has_somewhere_to_live: at least 25% of admissible coin-hours with V_oracle >= 5% of that cell's maker P&L AND oracle f <= 10% — a ceiling that is both material and reachable without declining most of the book
WHAT_COUNTS_declared_now_for_the_NEW_sta.why_these_numbers: 5% of maker P&L is the smallest ceiling that could survive any realistic sigma; f <= 10% is the reachability side. Both are set now, before any histogram exists, and are not adjusted afterwards.

WINDOW_CORRECTION_verified_at_the_code.consequence: the extra ~470 coin-hours are NOT already-consumed development evidence; they are outside the declared population, and surveying them would require a NEW declared era end, which is a declaration act and not mine
WINDOW_CORRECTION_verified_at_the_code.why: the era END is a DECLARED LITERAL per population (DECLARED_ERA_END_S), not the extent of the tape. The tape runs later — collector pids start 2026-08-26 — but this population does not declare it.

alpha_is_not_a_model_property: it is BOUNDED ABOVE by the book's adverse dispersion, so sigma/alpha is per-book and the 27.60% break-even is THIS book's number, not a constant
r_KEPT_AS_A_REPORTED_COLUMN: not dropped: it is what the specification was written against, the per-cell comparison between r and V_oracle is itself informative, and dropping it would leave this survey unable to correct the record

supersedes.why_the_pair: a bare filename cannot be verified and a resolver cannot follow it -- DE's resolver CRASHED on a bare-string supersedes (REV 54) and DA 91's census refuses to invent the link. Content is otherwise unchanged.

the_measured_hour_is_one_cell: 2026-08-24 13:50-14:50Z btc appears as ONE CELL and is not a reference point the others are compared against
touches_nothing_sealed: 09-01, 09-02 consumed economic reads; 09-03 accrued and unopened; none read
why_superseded: r is a ratio of two sums and DOES NOT DETERMINE whether an overlay can pay. The reviewer constructed three books on this book's own totals, varying only how adverse is DISTRIBUTED: r 18.63/18.65/18.99% with oracle ceilings of 0.00/10.62/22.19% and break-even thresholds of ~100/10.0/1.0%. Same r, opposite verdicts. A survey of r would have returned a distribution that answers nothing.
